top_story: A Houthi ballistic missile strike on a Yemeni government training camp on 19 October killed at least 53 people and wounded more than 200, sharply escalating Yemen’s renewed war and signaling a capacity to inflict mass casualties on state forces. The same day, the World Food Programme halted support for roughly 500,000 people in Gaza after funding shortfalls, deepening acute food insecurity and pushing winter famine risk higher for households already living on the edge. In the West Bank, the 18 October settler assault on European diplomats, a French mayor, and clergy in Taybeh during the olive harvest showed how violence around Palestinian land access is expanding beyond local intimidation and now directly tests Israel’s foreign relationships. Taken together, these developments show a region where armed actors are widening the space for coercion faster than governments and aid systems can protect civilians.
